Question_text: The speeds, v km/h, of 80 vehicles travelling along a road were recorded.The results are shown in the table. Calculate an estimate of the mean speed of the vehicles. Draw the cumulative frequency diagram. Use your cumulative frequency diagram to find an estimate for the median and the interquartile range.
Sub_topic: Estimate and interpret median, percentiles, quartiles and interquartile range from cumulative frequency diagrams

Question_text: Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B. Triangle A is mapped onto triangle C by a rotation 90° anticlockwise about (1, 1). Draw triangle C. Triangle A is mapped onto triangle D by the single transformation P. The matrix representing P is (2 0/0 2). Describe fully the single transformation P.
Sub_topic: Recognise, describe and draw reflection of shape in straight line
Recognise, describe and draw rotation of shape about centre through multiples of 90°
Recognise, describe and draw enlargement of shape from centre by scale factor
Recognise, describe and draw translation of shape by vector

Question_text: Rearrange m = 4n-3 to make n the subject. Solve these simultaneous equations. Show your working. Solve the equation 5x^2+3x-1=0.
Sub_topic: Solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square and by use of the quadratic formula

Question_text: Anton invests $6000 in an account for 5 years. The account has a compound interest rate of 2.5% per year. At the end of 5 years, he spends $4200 of this money on a family holiday to Malaysia. Anton changes $800 into Malaysian Ringgits (MYR) for his trip. The exchange rate is $1 = 3.16 MYR. He spends 2250 MYR and then changes the remaining money back into dollars ($). The exchange rate on his return is $1 = 3.27 MYR. How many dollars does he receive on his return? Anton invests $1500 in another account. The account has a compound interest rate of p% per year. At the end of 3 years, there is $1598.85 in the account. Calculate p.

A company makes and packages chocolate bars. These boxes are packed into cartons. Each carton is a cuboid with internal dimensions 30 cm by 28 cm by hcm. 80 boxes fill one carton exactly. The company sells the chocolate bars to shops for $0.70 each bar. A shop buys one carton of chocolate bars.
Sub_topic: Carry out calculations and solve problems involving surface area and volume of cuboid, prism, cylinder, sphere, pyramid, cone

Question_text: Draw the graph of y = (x^3/4) + 1 for -3 <= x <= 3. On the same grid, draw the graph of y = (1/3)x +1. Use your graph to find all the values of x where y = (1/3)x +1 crosses y = (x^3/4) -x +1. The values of x where y = (1/3)x +1 crosses y = (x^3/4) -x +1 are the solutions of the equation Ax^3 = Bx. Here are four equations. y=x^2-2x, y=2x^2-2, y=x^2+2x, y=2x^2. The graphs of three of these equations are sketched below. Write the correct equation below each graph.
Sub_topic: Construct tables of values, and draw, recognise and interpret graphs for functions of the following forms: axⁿ (includes sums of no more than three of these)
Solve associated equations graphically, including finding and interpreting roots by graphical methods

Question_text: The diagram shows a quadrilateral and part of a regular octagon. AB is a straight line. Form an equation in x and solve it to find x. P, Q, R, S and T are points on the circumference of a circle, centre O. PSQ = 32° and O lies on TQ. PS is parallel to QR and QR = RS. Find PÔT. Give a reason for each step of your working. Find QRS. Find TQS.
Sub_topic: Calculate unknown angles using sum of angles at a point (360°), on a straight line (180°), vertically opposite angles equal, triangle sum (180°), quadrilateral sum (360°)

Question_text: A display notice is made by removing a sector of a circle from a larger sector. Both sectors have an angle of 110°. The radii of the sectors are 80cm and 45 cm. Calculate arc length L. Calculate the area of this display notice. This diagram shows a display notice mathematically similar to the one in part (a). The radius of the larger sector is 32 cm. Calculate the area of this display notice.
Sub_topic: Carry out calculations involving arc length and sector area as fractions of circumference and area of circle

Question_text: A bag contains 10 tiles. There are 4 red tiles, x white tiles and the rest are blue. Two tiles are taken at random, without replacement, from the bag. Show that the probability that the tiles are both the same colour is (x^2-6x+21)/45. The probability the tiles are both the same colour is 16/45 Show that x^2-6x+5 = 0. Solve x^2-6x+5 = 0. There are more red tiles than white tiles in the bag. Find the probability that the first tile taken from the bag is blue.
Sub_topic: Calculate probability of combined events using sample space diagrams, Venn diagrams, tree diagrams
